name: Chung Ang University
overview:
Chung-Ang University (CAU) is a private institution with more than 30,000 students and nearly 1,000 faculty members.

It consists of 10 undergraduate colleges and 16 graduate schools. It has two campuses, in Seoul and Anseong, Korea.


Chung-Ang has a 6% acceptance rate, which is lower than most other Korean universities, showing that the acceptance process is very rigorous. This proves how prestigious the university is.


Founded in 1916, Chung-Ang University has traversed Korea's modern history by upholding its ideal of "Justice and Truth."


Since then, CAU has played a leading role in the education of the nation's intellectuals.


Fully accredited by the Korean Ministry of Education, CAU offers a wide range of bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral programs, including a law school, international MBA programs, and a medical school. Through the dynamic activities of these schools, Chung-Ang University has gained a leading recognition in the country.


In addition, CAU is recognized as the best in the country in the fields of pharmacy, culture, and art education.


As a prestigious private institution, Chung-Ang University is fully committed to guiding its Korean and international students to envision their life goals and realize their maximum potential in an increasingly competitive global society.


Having become one of Korea's top institutions of higher education since its establishment 90 years ago, Chung-Ang University, joined by the Doosan Group (one of Korea's leading global business groups), is rapidly making strides to achieve its goal of becoming a prestigious academic institution admired by the world.
administrative:
1. Application dossier


You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

The nominated students approved by CAU will receive an email from CAU explaining the different procedures. You should fill out and submit an online application (link to come). The online application system has been designed for Google Chrome, although it should be compatible with other browsers. If you are not able to complete the online application using a different browser, we recommend that you complete the application using Internet Explorer.

Your host university may ask you the following documents:


For non-OECD students :


  • Transcripts (available on your intra)
  • Financial Proof: Official document IN ENGLISH provided by the bank. You are required to bring the original copy together with you and submit the document to the international office of CAU. We recommend that your financial statement clearly states the USD equivalent of your bank balance. It must show a minimum balance of 12,000 USD. The required amount is subject to change according to the actual living cost every year. If your financial statement is not in your name, you must attach a letter from the bank account holder, together with the document. Please make sure that he/she includes his/her relationship with you in the letter and states that he/she will be financially responsible for you during your stay at CAU.


For everyone :

  • Copy of Passport
  • Digital Passport-size Photo (Image File): Size: 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm. Color photograph of face, front view, on white background, taken within the past six months


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Acceptance letter


After reviewing your application, CAU will send you these three documents (mandatory to apply for a visa):

  • Certificate of (University) Business Registration
  • Certificate of Admission
  • Certificate of Exchange Student


3. Visa and ARC (more information here and here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.

If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2025 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; the university will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4.Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


If you choose to live in the dormitory on campus, a Tuberculosis (TB) Test result in English or Korean, taken within 4 weeks before the dormitory move-in date is also required. The test should include student’s name, hospital/clinic name, date of the test, and test results in English/Korean. The test can be conducted in Korea, and in the form of a skin test, blood test, or X-ray. You'll need to bring the original test result to the dormitory move-in.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/coree-du-sud


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5.Prepare your arrival


For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.

You can create a Korean bank account on campus.

Please install KakaoTalk before arriving and bring cash.


6.Campus life


The Office of International Affairs organizes a GLAM buddy program, staffed by local CAU student volunteers, to help international students adjust to live in Korea.

The Office of International Affairs is located on the 2nd Floor of Building 310 and is open every day.


Nearby restaurants: the canteen, Chipoleon, Back mas, Boumbata, Delacourt, etc.

There are many clubs at CAU: sports (soccer, tennis), martial arts, music, artistic and cultural activities (literature clubs, calligraphy workshops, etc.).


Many activities dedicated to international students are organized, like the Exchange student booth, where exchange students can talk about their country and home university.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)


CAU provides on-campus orientation held the week before semester starts. Students are recommended to arrive at least a day before the orientation.


Students living on campus should arrive between the dormitory check in period. It is usually 2 to 3 days before the semester begins. The dormitory check in period will be announced later to accepted students via email. Any student arriving earlier than the official move-in date of the dormitory should find their own accommodation until they can move-in.


Students can apply for dormitory housing in June (subject to change). Students who wish to live in on-campus dormitory needs to apply through the online application page from a link provided by the Office of International Affairs (OIA), which will be sent when the dormitory dates are fixed. It is on a first-come, first-served basis. Please make sure to not miss the deadline as the dormitory availability is very limited and competitive.


Rooms have two or four beds. Please note that there are no kitchens, students usually eat out. Facilities include: LAN and Internet access, computer lab, phone line accessible in each room, TV with access to foreign TV channels, study rooms, a weight-training center, convenience stores.


Please note that there is a curfew at the dorms.


Cost per semester: about 760€ (without meal plan, which is mandatory). A deposit of about 65€ is needed.


Off-campus accommodation


If you'd rather live by yourself or choose who you live with, you can go for a shared apartment with roommates or an apartment of your own.
courses:
Credits


You will need to obtain 30 local credits, equivalent to 60 ECTS credits.

Chung Ang University allows you to take up to 19 credits in a single semester; however, Epitech recommends taking 15 credits per semester.

The allocation of credits across semesters is flexible and can be tailored to individual student needs (e.g., 12+18 or 15+15), as long as the total accumulates to 30 credits.


Academic calendar


  • 1st semester: From September to late December
  • 2nd semester: From March to late June


You will have to choose your classes as follows:

  • Option 1: 3 computer classes, 1 Korean class, 1 elective class (non-computer)
  • Option 2: 4 computer classes and 1 Korean class
  • Computer classes must be at the 3rd and 4th year level
  • Business classes, Korean language, and Korean culture classes are at the 1st year level



Department and Courses


You will study on the Seoul campus. Courses at Chung Ang are delivered in English and are typically theoretical.

Most classes share the same time slot, and some are held in different buildings, making it difficult to attend multiple classes in a timely manner. Therefore, pay attention to the class schedule and location when registering.

The list of classes taught in English is only available one month before the start of each semester and is subject to change year to year.


Registration


As an exchange student, you will be given priority in course selection. Follow the university’s instructions each time new modules open to avoid late registration and limited availability.

Class registrations occur in three installments at the beginning of each semester. Most classes tend to fill up by the second round of course registration. It is advisable to register for all desired courses and drop any unsuitable ones during the course drop-out period, which is one month after registration.

Class registration is on a first come, first served basis, often occurs early in the morning (European time) and fills up quickly due to limited space. We recommend staying awake or waking up early to secure your preferred classes.


Courses to choose


Please refer to this link: Courses Offered in English (Spring 2024).

The selected computer science classes must be at the third- and fourth-year (Bachelor) level. You are considered at Bachelor level at Chung Ang.

You are permitted to take classes from the College of Software and the College of General Education.

Please note that the ratio of IT to non-IT classes for the year should be 2:1. For example, you might take six classes from the College of Software (Department of Computer Science or Department of Artificial Intelligence) and four non-IT classes from the College of General Education or other departments. Any classes from other departments will be counted as non-IT, and you may be denied access if you are not from the respective department. Therefore, you cannot take as many or more non-computer science classes as computer science classes.

You must register for only third- and fourth-year classes, some of which may have prerequisites. Please consult the syllabus before registering.

Due to the low number of third and fourth year classes in the first semester, you may also choose the following first and second year courses, which have been approved by Epitech:

  • AI Design
  • Logic Circuit
  • Computer Architecture
  • Formal Language and Automata
  • Mathematics
  • Multicore Programming
  • Computer Application
  • Computer Application Practice
  • Database Design
  • Mobile Programming


Course Format and Workload


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "15 hours of classes and 8 hours of work a week (can be less). Classes last three hours in general. Please note that some courses require a level in maths, but it's not insurmountable."


Important notes


  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)


  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses


  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Visa: 126€
  • ARC: 20€
  • Insurance from university: 70€/month
  • Additional Insurance: 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage
  • Deposit for housing (dorms): 60€
  • Books and supplies: 200€, etc.


Estimated Monthly Budget


The local currency is the Won. 1 € = 1667,19 KRW (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


You should plan a budget of about 600€ a month, excluding rent.


Housing : 200-300€ (dorms)


Food : maximum 300€ / 5500KRW a meal (about 3.3€) at the cafeteria


Transportation : Rechargeable T-money card: 35€ / Metro: 0.7 to 1.20€ / Bus: 0.8 to 2€ / Monthly Climate card: 40€


Phone, internet : 12€ for unlimited 5G / Please note that if you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes 35G data in South Korea / Former students (2024-2025) have recommended Chingu Mobile.


Leisure : 100€+


These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)


  • Your visa allows you to work in South Korea up to 20 hours a week, Monday to Friday, during your study stay. However, to be able to work, you must change your visa to an S3 on site. Please note that it is still very difficult for a foreigner who does not speak Korean to find a part-time job.
  • You will receive an email from the partner university concerning a "scholarship". There are very few places, and you must make arrangements directly with the partner university.
  • Make sure to check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut. You'll be able to create a bank account in South Korea only when you have your ARC.
  • Useful apps: Coupang and Karrot (online shopping - equivalents of Amazon and Leboncoin), KakaoTalk and Google Translate/Papago/Deepl (communication), Baemin and Ubereats (food delivery), Uber, Naevar/Kakao maps because Google maps doesn't work (transport)
  • Use the Kakao Subway app, very useful for navigating Seoul’s subway. You can buy a metro card at a 7/11 or C&U (your student or bank card may also be used after about a month).
  • It is not compulsory to get a SIM card, as free wifi is often available in the streets. However, SIM cards provide access to more wifi, especially in the subway.
  • Korean people don't really cook and, rather, eat out a lot. You have options like restaurants (like pochas) and convenience stores which are open 24/7. Food is less expensive than in France. Typically, people share a few dishes.
